members.faq1A: During early access, membership is granted through invite and trial codes. We'll announce pricing clearly before any paid plans launch.
members.faq2Q: How is this different from the free tools?
members.faq2A: The free tools show the overall meta. The Advisor scores the specific augments you're offered — for your champion, your round, and your rerolls — which is the decision you actually face in game.
members.faq3A: Mayhem Oracle uses public data and your own manual inputs. It doesn't automate gameplay or access hidden information, and it isn't affiliated with Riot Games.
members.faq4A: Trial and invite access simply expire — there's nothing to cancel. You can request deletion of your account data anytime from the Contact page.

terms.intro: By using Mayhem Oracle (the "Service"), you agree to these terms. If you don't agree, please don't use the Service.

contact.title: Contact & About
contact.aboutBody: Mayhem Oracle turns ARAM Mayhem data into fast, practical decisions — champion tiers, augment scoring, and a draft Advisor. It's built by players, for players, and isn't affiliated with Riot Games.
contact.contactBody: Questions, feedback, a bug, or a membership request? Email us and we'll get back to you.
contact.responseNote: We're a small team, so replies can take a few days.
contact.dataBody: Game data is sourced from arammayhem.com and Riot's Data Dragon. Spotted something wrong? Let us know and we'll fix it.

privacy.title: Privacy & data use
privacy.intro: This policy explains what Mayhem Oracle collects, why, and the choices you have. We collect as little as possible.
privacy.s1Body: If you sign in, we store your account email (via Google sign-in) and your saved decision history. We collect basic, aggregated usage analytics to improve the Service.
privacy.s2Body: If you install the optional desktop collector, it uploads only de-identified match data — never your Riot ID, name, or chat.
privacy.s3Body: Public pages may show Google AdSense ads, gated behind your consent choice. You can decline personalized ads at any time using the consent banner.
privacy.s4Body: We use essential cookies for sign-in and your consent preference. Ad partners may set additional cookies only if you allow personalized ads.
privacy.s5Body: Raw collector uploads are deleted after 30 days; only de-identified aggregates are kept long-term. You can request deletion of your account data at any time.
privacy.s6Body: We use Google (sign-in and ads) and Supabase (authentication and storage) as service providers. We don't sell your personal data.
privacy.s7Body: Decline personalized ads in the consent banner, or contact us to access or delete your data.

about.title: About Mayhem Oracle
about.intro: Mayhem Oracle is an independent companion for making faster, better-informed decisions in League of Legends ARAM Mayhem.
about.whatBody: We turn current-patch game data into champion tiers, augment context, item information, patch notes, and practical tools for exploring a Mayhem draft.
about.dataBody: Our public data pipeline combines arammayhem, Riot's CommunityDragon and Data Dragon feeds, and the League of Legends wiki. It runs daily and refreshes the public catalog as the current patch and source data change.
about.contactBody: Have a question, found a data issue, or want to share feedback? Please get in touch.

method.title: How we rank
method.lead: What a letter means, where the numbers come from, and what they can't tell you.
method.sources_p: Win and pick rates come from arammayhem.com, fetched daily. That site doesn't say where its numbers come from; they appear to cover games on the Chinese servers, which we haven't been able to verify. It publishes rates, not game counts, and it publishes augment results for all champions together: its per-champion augment win rates are copies of each augment's overall rate, so we never show them as a champion's own.
method.estimand_p: The number is the win rate in games where the option was taken. That is an association, not a cause: stronger players and longer games can take some options more often. Each option is compared with the others in the same choice (lift), and its noise uses the set's average win rate, never its own.
method.letters_p: Options are grouped only where the data can order them, and each group takes the letter of its most modest well-measured member: S +3.5 points or more, A +1.5 or more, B within ±1.5, C −1.5 or less, D −3.5 or less. An outlined letter is thin, or depends on an unconfirmed unit in the source's data. Different letters are not a guarantee about every pair.
method.pick_h: Close calls on the Pick screen
method.pick_p: The Pick screen names a card only when it beats the next one by at least half a point with at least 80% certainty. Because the source has no per-champion augment results, each card also carries 2 points of champion-specific uncertainty, so about half of screens are a close call, and more for silver augments. That is the honest answer, not a gap in the screen.
method.patch_p: Letters follow the current patch's data. We tested carrying the last patch forward on new-patch days, and it did worse than the new data alone, so we don't.
method.cannot_h: What the numbers can't tell you
method.cannot_p: No game counts, no ± intervals, no per-champion augment results, no per-rank or per-stage splits. Build-order win rates count only games that finished the path, so paths are ranked against each other and never graded.
method.provenance: Data: arammayhem.com (source unstated; region unverified). Champion and item data: Riot Games (Data Dragon, CommunityDragon).
